newsitem.title: EGYPT: Hard labour for Egypt antiquities smugglers.
newsitem.headline: Hard labour for Egypt antiquities smugglers.

text.p: An Egyptian state security court on Sunday sentenced 12 men to jail, including three Britons in absentia, for stealing and smuggling antiquities to Britain, security sources said.
They said the court in Cairo sentenced three people, including a Briton, to 15 years in prison with hard labour, six men, including two Britons, to 10 years with hard labour.
Three people were given five years in jail with hard labour while the court acquitted three defendants of the charges, the sources said.
The names of the Britons were not available.
The Supreme Antiquities Council said in 1995 when the crime surfaced that some of the objects came to light when buyers took them to the British Museum in London for authentication.

Officials at the council said the antiquities, including statues, amulets and some papyrus scrolls more than 3,000 years old, were from the robbery of a storeroom in 1985. They had been in storage at Saqqara, the necropolis for the ancient city of Memphis, they said.
In connection with the case British police arrested and charged a policeman and two antique dealers with importing valuable stolen antiquities into Britain.
